data.title: Route Overview
paragraphs: Rajasthan’s monuments are spectacular, but this route is designed to keep human scale in the foreground. Udaipur begins with lake, palace, and miniature painting traditions; Jodhpur adds fort, market, textiles, and blue neighbourhoods; Jaisalmer shifts the palette toward sandstone and desert.

Road days are broken with meaningful stops rather than treated as lost time. Craft studios, village meals, stepwells, and desert-edge communities create continuity between the major cities, while heritage stays make architecture part of the experience after sightseeing ends.

data.title: Journey Standards & Inclusions
items: Heritage hotels selected for strong architecture and manageable old-city access.
Private vehicle throughout the intercity route, with slower scenic road days.
Craft visits arranged directly with respected workshops or family studios where possible.
Desert experiences designed to avoid crowded, high-volume entertainment camps.

data.title: Suggested Packing & Preparation
items: Light layers for warm days and cooler desert evenings.
Comfortable shoes for forts, old-city lanes, and uneven steps.
Sun protection and a reusable water bottle for exposed sightseeing.
A scarf for dust, sun, and temple visits.
One smart-casual outfit for heritage hotel dining or special evenings.

data.author: THE DESIGNER'S NOTEBOOK

data.title: DESERT SEASON NOTE
data.text: October to March offers the most comfortable conditions. Winter nights can be genuinely cool in the desert, while daytime sun remains strong and requires protection.

data.title: Beyond the Palace Facade
paragraphs: The great forts provide scale, but the journey’s emotional texture comes from smaller encounters: a painter’s hand, a market conversation, a courtyard breakfast, or sandstone turning gold at dusk.
Moving west from the lakes toward the Thar creates a clear sense of progression, with landscape and architecture becoming progressively drier, sharper, and more elemental.

items.question: Can this route be tailored to our preferred dates and pace?
paragraphs: Yes. Every Signature itinerary is a design framework, and we adjust nights, experiences, transport, and daily intensity around your interests and travel dates.

items.question: Will we stay inside historic properties?
paragraphs: Where the right property exists, yes. We balance heritage character with comfort, service, and practical access.

items.question: Is a camel safari included?
paragraphs: Not by default. Desert time can be designed around walking, jeep access, local communities, or a short ethical camel experience if desired.

items.question: Can Jaipur be added?
paragraphs: Yes. Jaipur works well as a pre-journey extension, although it changes the route into a longer Rajasthan circuit.

items.question: What is included when the final journey is quoted?
paragraphs: The final proposal clearly separates accommodation, private transport, guiding, arranged experiences, and any route-specific permits or specialist access.
items.listTitle: The exact inclusion list is confirmed before payment:
listItems: Chosen accommodation category and meal plan.
Confirmed guiding, hosted encounters, and ticketed experiences.
Any permits or special-access costs included in the final design.

items.question: How are reservations confirmed and scheduled?
paragraphs: Once the bespoke route, accommodation selection, and current supplier availability are approved, a 30% confirmation deposit secures the agreed services. The remaining balance is due 45 days before arrival unless the final proposal states otherwise.

items.question: What is the policy for date changes or cancellations?
paragraphs: We work directly with our partners to move dates whenever possible. Any non-refundable permits, transport tickets, or supplier penalties are passed through transparently.
listItems: 60+ days before arrival: deposit refund less confirmed non-refundable costs.
30–59 days before arrival: 50% refund or travel credit where supplier terms allow.
Less than 30 days before arrival: cancellation follows the confirmed supplier terms in your final proposal.
